purpose: Resolve the next capital, vehicle, investor-denominator, co-portfolio, governance-rights, transaction-specific vehicle, and ecosystem-banking fog around Erebor and Silent Ventures. The wave uses an audited SEC investment schedule to establish one actual post-opening Erebor security and to falsify exclusivity claims without inferring coordination from portfolio overlap.

method.null_hypothesis: ordinary private-capital formation through multiple investors and investment vehicles, with portfolio overlap reflecting broad innovation and defense exposure rather than common operating design
method.promotion_rule: An audited investment schedule may establish the holder, issuer, security, acquisition date, cost, reported value, and portfolio context it discloses. It does not establish the issuer's full capitalization, beneficial ownership, board or veto rights, private coordination, or the holder's influence over bank customers or operations.
method.portfolio_rule: Co-holdings in one investment fund are evidence of common portfolio custody only. They do not establish coordination, common design, intercompany transactions, shared governance, or operational integration.

records.proposition: Fundrise Innovation Fund held an actual Erebor Bank Series B preferred-stock investment by March 31, 2026.

sources.title: Fundrise Innovation Fund, LLC annual report for the year ended March 31, 2026

records.observation: The audited Fundrise Innovation Fund schedule lists 19 shares of Erebor Bank, N.A. Series B preferred stock, initially acquired February 20, 2026, with $5 million reported cost and $5 million reported fair value at March 31, 2026, representing 0.7 percent of fund net assets. The investment is classified as restricted, non-income-producing, and Level 3.
supports: an exact external investor, issuer, security class, acquisition date, cost, reported value, and portfolio weight
a transaction-specific capital record after Erebor's opening
a source-bounded expansion of the Erebor investor denominator
does_not_support: the bank's complete Series B size or capitalization
Fundrise beneficial ownership percentage
board, veto, information, observer, priority, or follow-on rights
coordination with Erebor organizers, Silent Ventures, Anduril, SpaceX, or another portfolio company
influence over bank customers, products, pricing, credit, or operations
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire Erebor's complete Series B capitalization, purchase and investor-rights agreements, stock ledger, beneficial ownership, board and observer rights, side letters, information and veto rights, transfer restrictions, allocation, proceeds, and every participating and declined investor.
records.falsifier: The audited schedule is corrected, the security does not represent an Erebor Bank equity interest, or the acquisition was reversed before the relevant date.

records.proposition: Erebor's recorded opening was followed within two weeks by the Fundrise Series B acquisition.

sources.title: Decisions on Bank Applications: Deposit Insurance
Fundrise Innovation Fund, LLC annual report for the year ended March 31, 2026

records.observation: The FDIC decisions table records an Erebor opening date of February 6, 2026. The Fundrise audited schedule records initial acquisition of Erebor Series B preferred stock on February 20, 2026.
supports: C3 public conversion followed by a private financing transaction
a precise chronology for testing capital conditions, proceeds, and public-risk/private-rights allocation
does_not_support: that opening approval caused or favored the Fundrise investment
that the investment satisfied a regulatory capital commitment
the identity of every Series B investor
preferential treatment, coordination, or extraction
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the Series B authorization, closing, use of proceeds, capital-plan and regulatory correspondence, pre-closing commitments, closing conditions, investor allocation, and matched de novo-bank post-opening financings.
records.falsifier: The dates or transaction identity are corrected materially, or the investment was unrelated to the bank's post-opening capitalization.

records.proposition: Erebor's post-opening equity was supplied exclusively by the currently named founder, defense-technology, and aligned venture network.

sources.title: Fundrise Innovation Fund, LLC annual report for the year ended March 31, 2026

records.observation: The audited schedule identifies Fundrise Innovation Fund as a Series B holder. Fundrise Advisors, LLC is disclosed as the fund's SEC-registered adviser and a subsidiary of Rise Companies Corp.; neither entity is part of the current M-04B named aligned-capital set.
supports: an investor outside the currently named aligned-capital denominator
a requirement to expand the capital denominator beyond founder and defense-network names
does_not_support: complete independence of every Fundrise relationship
absence of named-network investors in the same round
absence of side letters, syndication, referrals, or co-investment
ordinary or exceptional treatment of the investor
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Freeze the complete Series B investor and beneficial-owner denominator, identify every direct and indirect vehicle, and test syndication, allocation, referral, rights, and preexisting relationships symmetrically.
records.falsifier: Operative closing records show that Fundrise held only as nominee or conduit for a currently named aligned investor or had no independent economic interest.

records.proposition: One independently disclosed innovation fund's simultaneous exposure to Erebor, Anduril, and SpaceX establishes common operating design among those portfolio companies.

sources.title: Fundrise Innovation Fund, LLC annual report for the year ended March 31, 2026

records.observation: The same audited fund schedule reports exposure to Anduril, SpaceX, Erebor, and many unrelated technology companies through direct securities, special-purpose vehicles, and co-investment vehicles. The fund's disclosed purpose and diversified portfolio structure provide an ordinary investment explanation for co-holdings.
supports: a matched control for shared-investor and shared-portfolio reasoning
evidence that co-holdings can arise through broad innovation-fund allocation without operational integration
a requirement to distinguish direct securities from SPVs and co-investment vehicles

absence of common investors elsewhere

neutrality or independence of every investment decision
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Compare complete innovation-fund portfolios, security types, vehicles, investment dates, governance rights, board roles, syndicates, transactions, customer relationships, and noncoordinated controls before using shared capital as evidence of design.
records.falsifier: Transaction and governance records show that the co-holdings were deliberately assembled under common operating agreements, governance, intercompany transactions, or coordinated strategy.

records.proposition: The currently identified Erebor and Silent Ventures capital records establish a coordinated private capital and banking organ that reproduces the broader founder-controlled system.
records.observation: Wave 08 establishes one actual external Erebor Series B investment, a post-opening financing chronology, an outside-the-current-set investor, an ordinary diversified co-portfolio comparator, exact Silent Fund II formation hierarchy, and unresolved Silent transaction rights and Erebor banking traffic. It does not establish common governance, capital exclusivity, banking transactions, portfolio-company coordination, or reproduction of missing system functions.
supports: continued transaction-specific testing of capital, governance, banking, and reproduction propositions
does_not_support: system-wide coordinated capital organ
exclusive aligned financing
Erebor as an operating ecosystem rail
